editorial:
Imagine being ripped away from your family at twelve years old and sold into a world of pain. That is exactly what happens to Malia, the daughter of a strong wrestler in Sudan. You will feel her fear as she is taken by militia and sold to a mean woman in Khartoum. The movie follows her journey from the mountains of Sudan to the streets of London, where she thinks she has found safety, but instead finds a new kind of prison. It is a heavy story that makes you realize how some people can be truly cruel, but it also shows how strong the human spirit is when you just want to go home.

The acting is what really sells this story, making you feel every bit of Malia's sadness and hope. While the movie moves a bit slow in some parts, the emotional payoff is worth it. You should definitely watch this if you like true stories that open your eyes to the world. Since it is a drama, you want the best picture to see the details of the different locations.
endingExplained: In the end, Malia finds a kind person who helps her realize she is not alone. She manages to escape her captors and get the help she needs from the authorities. The movie wraps up by showing her struggle to reunite with her father, Bah. The biggest punch comes at the very end with a text screen telling you that thousands of people are still trapped in similar slave situations right now in Britain.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves powerful true stories about survival and human rights.
